Notes on Spectral Theory
text:
Bounded Operators
Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space over \(\C\). Recall our global macro test: \(x \in \R^n\) and \(\inner{u}{v}\).

Definition 1 (Spectrum) Let \(T \in \End(H)\). The spectrum of \(T\), denoted \(\Spec(T)\), is the set of all \(\lambda \in \C\) such that \(T - \lambda I\) is not invertible.

Matrix Examples

0 & 1 \\
-1 & 0
\end{pmatrix}\]
The piecewise cases environment works as expected:
\[f(x) = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } x \in \Q, \\
0 & \text{if } x \notin \Q.
\end{cases}\]

Definition 2 (Hilbert Space) A Hilbert space \(H\) is a complete inner product space with an inner product \(\inner{x}{y}\).


Theorem 1 (Spectral Theorem) Let \(T\) be a compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space \(H\).

We apply Definition 2 to prove Theorem 1.

About Me
About Me
text:
Bio
I am a currently a graduate student in the Department of Statistics at UW-Madison. I value purposeful and humble pedagogy, one that acknowledges that we are at once all students and teachers. I believe this value cannot be divorced from a praxis that continues to express joy, inspires solidarity, and romanticizes the process rather than valuing only the conclusion; where we might otherwise measure learning and living solely materially.

title: About Me
text:
Research Interests

Probability Theory (e.g., limit theorems, “classical results”)
Extreme Value Theory (e.g., regular variation, max-limits, risk)
Stochastic Dynamics (e.g., SDEs, Martingales, Ergodicity/path properties)
